title: Prompt about unauthorized Thunderbolt devices
head: 6caba24cac4b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The shipped Bolt daemon can already authorize and enroll new devices with no menu choice on IOMMU-protected hosts
leads.consequence: For a pending peripheral on an IOMMU-protected domain with Bolt's default AuthMode enabled, boltd auto-enrolls and authorizes the device upon its udev add event, before this 30-second poll can show a consent prompt. The sysfs scanner subsequently sees authorized != 0 and does not notify. This contradicts the feature's explicit-only security premise, although it remains true that this PR's own boltctl authorize/enroll calls follow a choice. Enforcing approval would require addressing Bolt's auto-enrollment policy, not just adding a notification.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q1: confirmed from bolt 0.9.11 source

leads.summary: Another open Thunderbolt security PR collides in first-run and makes this PR's permanent-enrollment choice fail when its protection is enabled
leads.consequence: #11874 independently enables its Thunderbolt approval watcher and this PR enables the notify service, path and timer. Both can present a prompt for the same blocked device. Its Bolt configuration sets AuthMode=disabled: boltctl authorize remains possible, but this PR's 'Authorize permanently (enroll)' calls Bolt's EnrollDevice, which is rejected when that mode is disabled; the menu reports a generic failure and leaves the notification state. Both edit the same last entries of first-run's unit list and a three-way merge has conflict markers, so simply picking either side loses the other's registrations.
leads.triage: conflict corroborated by Opus (P8); AuthMode behaviour via follow-up Q2; confirmed; authorize-then-enroll workaround narrowed after self-check F1

leads.summary: The migration records itself complete even when all three unit starts fail
leads.consequence: In an active graphical session, each failed systemctl start prints an error and sets start_error, but the script finishes by printing the next-login warning and returns zero. omarchy-migrate therefore creates its marker and does not retry the explicit starts on subsequent updates. The enabled units will still be pulled in on the next login if they can start then, but a persistent failure receives no repeat migration diagnostic. Return nonzero (or explicitly schedule a retry) after the warning if this is meant to block marking the migration complete.
leads.triage: behavioural, by design; dropped: the migration prints the errors and a next-login warning, and the units are enabled

leads.summary: Pruning only observes snapshots, so a quick disconnect and reconnect can suppress future notification indefinitely
leads.consequence: A device already present in notified can disconnect and reconnect with the same unique_id between 30-second scans. Neither scan sees the absence, so the state entry is never pruned and the next unauthorized connection is invisible even though the code promises a fresh notification after disconnection. If the Thunderbolt bus directory was absent at a scan, the early exit also skips pruning; a subsequent connection with the same UUID remains suppressed. A real removal/connection event source or state tied to the device's current connection, rather than just its UUID, is needed for the stated behavior.
leads.triage: minor edge case of polling; dropped as low value

leads.summary: First-run's per-unit-loop PR would drop these three new registrations unless its list is reconciled
leads.consequence: #10582 rewrites the one systemctl enable call as a units=(...) loop, with no omarchy-thunderbolt-notify.service, .path or .timer. It is not stacked on this PR and their own-base three-way merge conflicts. If its loop wins without adding all three, fresh installs will complete first-run without enabling this feature even with all PKGBUILD entries present; #10582's tests enumerate only the earlier units and would not catch that omission. Add all three to that loop and its assertion if the PRs are combined.
leads.triage: factual, already raised in the second review; author acknowledged; not repeated

leads.summary: The changed package-defaults test never inspects the dev PKGBUILD when the stable recipe exists, nor does it inspect packaged results
leads.consequence: With both recipes in the normal omarchy-pkgs checkout, the test always chooses omarchy-settings/PKGBUILD, never omarchy-settings-dev/PKGBUILD. A plausible regression deleting only the three new installs from the dev recipe passes this new assertion. Even the stable check only searches source and destination strings, so code under an inoperative conditional still passes. Test both package variants against an actually staged source/artifact, or separately assert both unit sets rather than trusting substring presence.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus (config-test.sh:138-143); nit, kept in REPORT only

leads.summary: The notification-hardening PR turns a restored Thunderbolt toast into a dead click while this PR's cache prevents a replacement
leads.consequence: #13312 intentionally strips execArgv from persisted notifications when the shell restarts. If a waiting Thunderbolt toast was delivered before that restart, this PR keeps its UUID in notified, so future timer checks do not send a fresh toast with a current token. The restored toast still says 'Click to review', but its click no longer opens omarchy-thunderbolt: Service.qml falls through to focus the sender app instead and dismisses it. A subsequent scan still treats the UUID as notified, leaving no actionable alert unless the user knows and runs the CLI manually. Re-send on shell generation change or have this toast explicitly explain its CLI fallback.
leads.triage: factual part verified by coordinator (#13312 description); behavioural via follow-up Q3; confirmed from source

leads.summary: Changing the Thunderbolt opt-out flag mid-session does not start or stop the polling timer
leads.consequence: If thunderbolt-auth-off exists when timers.target first starts, the timer's ConditionPathExists skips its activation. Deleting the file later with the existing toggle command does not reevaluate the inactive timer or start the path/service, so authorization prompts remain absent until a unit restart or new login. Conversely, creating the flag while the timer is already active prevents the service scan but does not stop 30-second timer wakeups. Couple the opt-out toggle to explicit systemctl --user stop/start or document that the choice takes effect on next login.

leads.summary: The public feature description still promises a kernel instant path trigger and a strict authorized == 1 check
leads.consequence: Users and maintainers are told that connecting a device fires an instant sysfs path notification and that the reviewer verifies exactly authorized == 1, while the unit itself says kernfs does not deliver the create notification and the check allows 2 as authorized. Update the description to distinguish timer-delayed detection and successful 1/2 readback. This is documentation, not a new runtime failure.

limits: No live Thunderbolt controller, Bolt daemon, or graphical user session was accessed; H1 and H2 are corroborated from bolt 0.9.11 and kernel v6.16 source. The sandboxed runs use synthetic bus trees and systemctl stubs. A full './test/cli' run in the isolated repo passed the new command metadata checks but stopped at an unrelated missing theme fixture; test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh and systemd-test.sh passed. No upstream comments or review discussion were read.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on the [second review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12510#issuecomment-5858204486) and [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12510#issuecomment-5879246450), at `6caba24c`: one merge-order defect remains.

- **Resolved:** packaging (with #713), timer condition, device names, path comment, `run_suite.sh`.
- **Partly:** line 65 still says "this session".
- **Still present:** #11874 overlap, stale description.
- **Corrected:** two second-review statements (Details).

### First-run fails if this lands before omarchy-pkgs#713

Dev builds track `quattro`. Without #713 they ship none of the three units, so `enable --now` in `enable-user-units.sh` exits 1, nothing is enabled and first-run repeats at every login until the units ship.

**Suggested change:** Merge omarchy-pkgs#713 first or together; say so in the PR description.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at omarchy-pkgs master, passes with #713)</summary>

Run from an omarchy checkout at `6caba24c`, with an omarchy-pkgs checkout next to it (`../omarchy-pkgs`), once at current omarchy-pkgs `master` (`5a49a3f`, without #713) and once at the #713 head (`80db2be`). `config-test.sh` needs `jq`, `lua` and `python3`. The second script builds `omarchy-settings` with that checkout's own `package()` (only ImageMagick is stubbed), then runs an offline `systemctl --root` enable of the exact unit list in `install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh`.

`first-run-offline.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from an omarchy checkout at 6caba24c. $1: an omarchy-pkgs checkout.
# Builds omarchy-settings with that checkout's package(), then enables the
# first-run unit list offline against the packaged user units.
set -u
pkgs=${1:?usage: first-run-offline.sh /path/to/omarchy-pkgs}
work=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$work/src" "$work/pkg" "$work/bin"
ln -s "$PWD" "$work/src/omarchy"
# Icon thumbnails are irrelevant here; stand in for ImageMagick.
printf '#!/bin/bash\nout=${!#}; out=${out#PNG32:}; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"; : >"$out"\n' >"$work/bin/magick"
chmod +x "$work/bin/magick"
(
  set -e
  export CARCH=x86_64 srcdir="$work/src" pkgdir="$work/pkg" PATH="$work/bin:$PATH"
  source "$pkgs/pkgbuilds/omarchy-settings/PKGBUILD"
  package
) >/dev/null
echo "package() exit: $?"
ls "$work/pkg/usr/lib/systemd/user" | grep thunderbolt || echo "no Thunderbolt units packaged"
# owed.service ships in the owe package, not omarchy-settings; stand in for it.
printf '[Service]\nExecStart=/bin/true\n[Install]\nWantedBy=default.target\n' >"$work/pkg/usr/lib/systemd/user/owed.service"
units=$(sed -n '/enable --now/,/^$/p' install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh | grep -o '[a-z0-9-]*\.\(service\|path\|timer\)')
systemctl --root="$work/pkg" --global enable $units >/dev/null 2>"$work/err"
echo "systemctl enable exit: $?"
grep -v -e '^Created symlink' -e 'is added as a dependency' "$work/err"
echo "links created: $(find "$work/pkg/etc/systemd/user" -type l 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
```

systemd 261.2 (`systemctl --root`). The build at `master` succeeds, so nothing in the package build flags the missing units.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Merge order:** the dev lane repins the `quattro` tip and merges green builds automatically; a build without #713 succeeds (its `package()` exits 0 with no Thunderbolt units). `config-test.sh` also fails against omarchy-pkgs `master` until #713 merges (reproducer above).

**Still present**
- **#11874:** a trial merge with its head conflicts in `enable-user-units.sh` (reproducer below), and both PRs still prompt for the same device. #11874 also sets bolt's `AuthMode = disabled` when its protection is on (its default), under which "Authorize permanently (enroll)" fails with "Failed to authorize" while "Authorize for this session" works (bolt 0.9.11 `bolt-manager.c:1609-1614`). Enrolling after `boltctl authorize` avoids the error, but with AuthMode disabled bolt does not re-authorize stored devices on reconnect (`bolt-manager.c:1430-1444`), so the permanent option would need #11874's own approval path. Source-only.
- **State comment:** `bin/omarchy-thunderbolt-check:65` still says "never notified about this session", while lines 118-122 now say the state persists across logins.
- **Description:** it still describes an instant `PathChanged` trigger and "Verifies `authorized == 1`", and does not mention #713.

**Related open PR #13312** (source-only): it clears the click action of toasts restored after a shell restart. The Thunderbolt toast is critical, so if it is still on screen it is restored, and a click then only dismisses it. Because the device stays in the notified state, no fresh toast follows while it stays connected. Keeping the state in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or re-sending when the shell session changes, would limit this.

**Corrections to the second review**
- Dropping the timer condition brings back 30 s polling on every install, aarch64 included, not only x86_64.
- "`boltctl` runs only after a menu choice" is too broad: a read-only `boltctl list` runs when nothing is waiting. Accurate: the scripts make no authorizing `boltctl` call without a choice. Separately, with its default configuration, stock bolt auto-enrolls new devices on hosts with IOMMU DMA protection (`bolt-manager.c:1653-1687`), so there the prompt appears only in narrower cases, such as a device stored with policy `manual`, AuthMode disabled or a failed auto-enroll (source-only).

**Verified** (sandbox; real gum 2.0.0 `style`, `gum choose` stubbed)
- Devices named `-x` or `--help` enroll, print the name and send the success toast. A later device in the same run is still offered.
- An empty `device_name` shows the unique id in the toast and menu.
- Esc, Ctrl-C and Skip make no `boltctl` call.
- Pruning, replug toasts, `authorized=2` and the missing-name fallback behave as at `2ae0d797`.
- `./test/shell` and `./test/cli` show the same results at `2ae0d797` and `6caba24c` (with #713 as the omarchy-pkgs checkout).
</details>
